Feelings: some learners have lived through a hurricane, a flood, or an earthquake. Keep the stories in the lesson invented. Never ask about real disasters. "I don't want to say" is always OK.

runs.t: By the end of class, you can do these six things.
I can understand a weather alert.
A big storm will arrive tonight.
I can say what will happen if….
I can ask What will you do if…?
I can make predictions with probably and maybe.
I can give safety tips with should.
I can fill in a Ready Plan card.

slides.notes:
Read each goal slowly. Learners repeat.
Goal 1: understand a short weather forecast and a weather alert. Goal 2: If the power goes out, I'll use a flashlight. Goal 3: What will you do if…?
Goal 4: It will probably rain. It probably won't snow. Goal 5: simple safety tips with should (review). Goal 6: read a weather alert text and fill in a simple "My Ready Plan" card.
"We check at 7:25" = the Progress Check. It is not a test grade.

Listening script (the audio is coming soon; until then, read it aloud with a volunteer at a normal, friendly speed):
Narrator: Lesson six. Listening. First, listen to a weather alert on the radio. Then listen to two roommates, Nadia and Ben.
Narrator: This is a weather alert for Green County. A big storm will arrive tonight at about nine o'clock. There will probably be strong wind and heavy rain. The power will probably go out in some areas.
Nadia: Ben, did you hear that? A storm is coming tonight.
Ben: Yes. If the power goes out, we won't have any lights.
Nadia: Do we have a flashlight?
Ben: We have one, but it doesn't have batteries. I'll buy some after work.
Nadia: Good. And if the power goes out, the fridge won't work.
Ben: Then we'll eat the food in the fridge first! I'll buy bottled water, too.
Nadia: Great. Should we buy candles?
Ben: No, candles aren't safe. We'll use the flashlight. And I'll charge our phones before nine.
Nadia: OK. If the storm is really bad, will we go to work tomorrow?
Ben: Probably not. It'll probably rain all night. I'll check the forecast in the morning.
Narrator: That's the end of the listening.

Step 5 · 7:00–7:12 · Talk Time: What If? Chain + Ready Plan · 12 min. Groups of 3–4.
Round 1, the chain (5 min): the first person says a sentence from a start card (If it snows tomorrow, I'll stay home.). The next person starts with the end of that sentence (If I stay home, I'll cook soup.), and so on around the group. Keep going until the chain stops, then start a new card. Each click shows the next step.
Model with two learners (1 min): "If it snows tomorrow, I'll stay home." → Learner 1: "If I stay home, I'll watch TV." → Learner 2: "If I watch TV, I'll…" Laugh at funny chains; that's fine.
Start cards: 1 If it snows tomorrow, I'll stay home. 2 If the power goes out tonight, I'll use a flashlight. 3 If it's very hot this weekend, I'll go to the beach. 4 If the bus doesn't come, I'll walk to work. 5 If it rains on Saturday, I'll clean my house. 6 If I win some money, I'll buy a new car.
Useful: If I…, I'll… • Then… • That's funny! • Your turn.
